2027 Honda John McGuinness CBR1000RRR & Lake Ontario Riding

Aug 31, 2026 Michael Le Pard News, What’s New

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 6:28
Instaread

Let’s get this silliness out of the way, Lake Ontario will never be referred to as “lake america”, it’s been mapped Lake Ontario since the 16th Century before the USA existed. I was born a mile from it’s shores. But what Lake Ontario does offer is incredible motorcycle riding, roads, wineries, weather and scenery. John McGuinness would love it aboard the new 2027 Honda CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP Limited Edition John McGuinness 30th Anniversary Replica and you would too.

In fact, the beautiful lap around Lake Ontario normally would take 12 hours and 32 minutes, but for Isle of Man TT winner John McGuinness with his 30 years of racing experience it would take just 4 hours and 19 minutes (average speed of 132 mph (213 km/h). That’s just an afternoon ride to see Lake Ontario’s sights, sounds and curvey roads.

In this week’s special Total Motorcycle article super feature, I highlight the new 2027 Honda CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP Limited Edition John McGuinness 30th Anniversary Replica as well as the beautiful motorcycling roads around Lake Ontario.

 

Limited Edition John McGuinness 30th Anniversary Replica CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP

  • Detailed reproduction of the 30th anniversary Superbike that John McGuinness MBE rode at this year’s Isle of Man TT races
  • Only 15 to be produced, with full Race Replica livery plus a host of parts and accessories. Also includes an exclusive handover lap of the TT course with John McGuinness MBE
  • Retail price of £37,730; orders can be placed upon invitation

John McGuinness MBE and the Honda Fireblade are synonymous with the Isle of Man TT races. Aside from the first 130mph lap and the complete dominance for almost a decade including an emphatic Senior TT win in 2015, this year John and Honda celebrated 30 years of TT racing with a superbike livery harking back to John’s very first TT race in 1996.

In honour of 30 incredible years of TT racing, Honda UK has produced a limited run of road legal replicas of John’s superbike, as ridden in the 2026 Senior TT. Just fifteen lucky Honda customers will have the chance to own a CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP JM 30th Anniversary.

Alongside the motorcycle, owners will also receive a signed McGuinness replica KYT helmet which will be handed over in an exclusive meet and greet on the Isle of Man. If owners choose to, they can add their first 37 ¾ miles to the bike around the TT course following John. Creating a never to be repeated memory with a road racing hero, on the very roads on which the legend was created.

 

ABOUT THE BIKE

The 2026 CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP was the star of the Superbike show at the 2026 Isle of Man TT races. In his 30th year of racing at the TT, John McGuinness MBE was honoured by Honda Racing UK with a racing livery that nodded all the way back to where it began. The Honda RS250 from 1996 displayed John’s career long sponsor and friend Paul Bird Motorsport. The distinctive green number board used on the 2026 bike is a period correct throwback to what was used in the lightweight class ’96. With split throttle bodies, a 999cc liquid cooled inline four cylinder engine producing 214bhp, a swingarm derived directly from the RC213V-S, HRC developed aero, a six-axis internal measurement unit and an Akrapovic developed Titanium exhaust leaves the owner in no doubt at all of the potential the motorcycle has.

Each John McGuinness 30th Anniversary Replica CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP also gets:

  •      Full Race Replica Livery
  •      Individually numbered headstock plaque
  •      Honda Genuine Accessories – Tall Screen, Seat Cowl & HRC Oil Filler Cap
  •      GB Racing Engine Cover Set
  •      Evotech Radiator Guard, Brake Lever Guard and Paddock Stand Bobbins
  •      Fitted with Metzeler Tyres with OE Tyres provided as spare
  •      Only 15 to be sold, by invitation, with a retail price of £37,730

And There’s more. Alongside the bike itself, the package also includes:

  • Exclusive meet and greet handover event on the Isle of Man, with the chance to ride a lap with John.
  • KYT Limited Edition John McGuinness replica Helmet KX-1 – signed by John in the customer’s preferred size
  • Gee-Tech rear Paddock Stand with 30th Anniversary Logo
  • Custom Garage Mat

 

Unfortunately, the new longest named motorcycle model in the history of motorcycles, the 2027 Honda CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP Limited Edition John McGuinness 30th Anniversary Replica is only sold in the UK for now with a bigger than life price of £37,730. And there’s only 15 of them… which is good as I run out of breath just saying the model name!!

Lake Ontario Existed before the USA

Ok, so let’s dig into this silliness about renaming Lake Ontario, a lake that is shared 50/50 between the boarders of Canada and the USA. Here are 3 maps showing Lake Ontario from 1703, 1757 and 1774. So far Google and the US Mapping Service has changed the name (as I far as I know to date), shame on them. We all know that Google sucks as a company anyways since they got rid of their “Do No Evil” mantra years ago.

 

In 1703, King Louis XIV had this map drawn. There were no USA. But there was Canada, Quebec and Lake Ontario. France carried on the name given to the water expanse by the people who lived in Canada at the time. As Ontario was good enough for all the Kings and Queens, Prime ministers and Presidents since.

 

President Donald Trump signs an executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America.” pic.twitter.com/uOnLpw53t6
